title: Quasar Life — Project Helix: Concurrency & Cost Sweep
content:
Executive summary:

This note summarizes a week-long benchmarking sweep we ran for Quasar Life (Project Helix) to validate latency, throughput, and unit-cost behavior for their customer-facing document-answering endpoint. Goal was to identify operating points that meet a 200ms P95 interactive target for short-chat queries (<= 64 tokens) while minimizing token cost under expected bursty traffic (1–300 qps).

High-level result: with the recommended configuration (dedicated pool of 4 H100-80GB nodes, dynamic batching target 8 tokens, prefix KV cache enabled, int8-quantized model variant), we achieved: P50=45ms, P95=182ms, P99=320ms at 150 sustained qps with end-to-end request/response sizes typical for Helix test-set (~28 tokens input, ~48 tokens output). This delivered an estimated hosted-like unit cost of $0.011 per 1k output tokens (model+infrastructure amortization estimate used in the spreadsheet). Tail behavior is the principal remaining risk: microburst recovery (qps spikes > 500) produced transient P99s up to 900ms unless burst capacity/fallback configured.

Test environment and config:

- Model: Quasar-3B-family baseline (decoder-only), production variant + int8 quantized variant used for cost runs.
- Redwood runtime: Dedicated pool (experimental patch 2029-05-b) with continuous batching and prefix cache hooks enabled.
- Hardware tested: H100-80GB (primary), fallback H100-64GB (simulated).
- Instances in pool: 2, 4, 8 node configurations evaluated.
- Autoscaling: cold-start penalty experiments with scale-from-0 disabled/enable.
- Network: colocated region (us-west2); average network RTT measured 6–12ms.
- Metrics collected: end-to-end latency (client->response), model-inference-only latency, batch sizes, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, QPS, tokens/s, and cost model inputs (instance-hour, GPU price estimate, mem/disk).

Workloads and methodology:

We generated three synthetic workload profiles derived from Quasar telemetry:
1) Interactive-small (median request tokens 22, response median 40) — 60% of traffic.
2) Long-form (input 120 tokens, response 256 tokens) — 10% of traffic (rare but cost-sensitive).
3) Microburst traffic (sustained baseline 40 qps with spikes to 600 qps lasting 30–90s).

For each pool size and model variant, we ramped QPS from 10 to peak in 30-minute windows and recorded percentiles over 5s/1m sliding windows. Cold-start tests: drain-to-zero then rehydrate to 50 qps. Each configuration repeated 3 times for statistical stability.

Key raw numbers (Interactive-small profile, H100, 4 nodes, quantized variant):
- Sustained QPS test at 150 qps:
  - p50 end-to-end: 45ms
  - p95 end-to-end: 182ms
  - p99 end-to-end: 320ms
  - mean GPU utilization (per node): 62%
  - average observed batching: 5.6 requests/batch
  - prefix cache hit-rate: 37% (initial TTL 45s)
  - estimated cost: $0.011 per 1k output tokens (model compute + infra apportioned)

- Sustained QPS test at 300 qps (same config but 8-node pool):
  - p50: 48ms; p95: 210ms; p99: 410ms; batching 7.1; cache hit-rate 34%; GPU util 75%

Microburst behavior:
- Spike to 600 qps with current autoscaling (scale-from-2, max 12) produced P99s up to 900ms and occasional 503s when queue overflowed on a subset of nodes.
- Enabling a 2-node warm reserve and burst overflow to a lower-cost model variant reduced peak P99s to ~480ms and eliminated 503s in 6/6 runs.

Cold-starts and warmup:
- Scale-from-0 cold starts produced median first-response latencies of 1.6–2.1s depending on model variant.
- Observed cache warmup slope: prefix cache hit-rate increased from 2% to stable ~38% over first 8 minutes at steady traffic; this meaningfully reduced average latency after warmup.

Quantization effects (int8):
- Inference latency per-token reduced by ~12–18% vs FP16 on matched batch sizes for small responses.
- Quality: automated BLEU-like and retrieval QA checks showed negligible degradation for Helix test prompts (<0.6% score drop); we flagged 3 prompt families where hallucination rates increased slightly — see Appendix B for prompt examples.

Cost breakdown (conservative estimates):
- Baseline (FP16) @ 4 nodes, 150 qps: $0.017 per 1k output tokens.
- Quantized (int8) same config: $0.011 per 1k output tokens (~35% reduction).
- Using model variant fallback during 80% of microburst window (cheap small model) pushes effective cost down to $0.008 per 1k tokens for the burst window, at the expense of degraded quality in 2% of queries.

Analysis and interpretation:

1) Meeting SLA: 200ms P95 is achievable for the interactive profile with 4 H100-80GB nodes and quantized model if traffic is primarily in the interactive-small bucket and prefix cache warms. Without quantization, hitting the 200ms P95 requires either 6+ nodes or accepting higher cost.

2) Tail risk: P99 and microburst recovery are the highest operational risks. Two mitigations worked well in tests: a) reserve 1–2 warm nodes to accept immediate bursts, and b) configure burst overflow policy to route excess requests to a compatible smaller variant (model downgrading) with automatic tagging to allow quality monitoring. Both reduce 503s and cap P99.
3) Cost/quality tradeoffs: int8 quantization delivered the best cost reduction while preserving quality across the bulk of Helix prompts. For the small set of sensitive prompts, we recommend a per-route policy that pins FP16 and disables automatic downgrade.

4) Prefetch/prefix cache policy: TTL of 45–60s gave the best latency gains for Quasar's traffic shape. Cache hit-rate is correlated with steady-user sessions; for users who issue multi-turn sessions the benefit compounds. We recommend enabling prefix cache with per-tenant TTL configuration.

Recommendations (practical operating plan):

- Short term (POC -> pilot):
  1) Deploy 4-node dedicated pool H100-80GB with quantized model variant as baseline. (Owner: Priya)
  2) Configure 2-node warm reserve and burst overflow to Quasar-compact model. (Owner: Liam)
  3) Set prefix cache TTL to 60s and monitor hit-rate for first 48h of pilot. (Owner: Diego)
  4) Instrument per-route quality checks for the 3 flagged prompt families; create an exemption rule to force FP16 for those routes. (Owner: Sofia)

- Medium term (pilot -> production):
  1) Expand pool to 6 nodes only if steady utilization >70% over 24h and P95 increases.
  2) Add automated rollback policy if microburst P99 exceeds 700ms more than twice in a 12h window.
  3) Run A/B of quantized vs FP16 on 5% of live traffic for 7 days to validate production quality.

Action items and open questions:

- [ ] Priya: apply pool config and upload new autoscaling policy to JIRA-HE-1243 (due 2029-05-22).
- [ ] Liam: implement burst overflow routing test and tag github PR for review (github.com/redwood/helix-load-tests/pull/27).
- [ ] Diego: produce a 24h dashboard showing prefix cache hit-rate, p95, p99, and 503 counts (due 2029-05-24).
- [ ] Sofia: draft per-route exemption rule for sensitive prompts and circulate to Quasar for approval.
- Q: Quasar asked about tolerable quality delta for the compact variant — recommend we prepare live-human evals for the 3 prompt families before enabling automatic downgrade.

Appendices:

A) Full numeric tables for all runs are in s3://redwood-results/helix/2029-05/summary.csv and linked_artifacts above.

B) Prompt families flagged for quality review (short descriptions):
  - Family A: multi-step diagnostic reasoning with domain-specific tokens (sensitive to word-choice).
  - Family B: regulatory compliance phrasing (precision required).
  - Family C: long-context summarization edge-cases (early truncation leads to omission).

C) Test scripts used: github.com/redwood/helix-load-tests (see README for reproduction steps).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working report intended for Quasar SRE and the Redwood deployment team. Many runs were exploratory — numbers are final for the configurations called out, but variations may be needed for different traffic mixes. If approved, we'll run the 7-day production A/B and prepare a final cost forecast for Quasar's projected 6-month volume.
